paragraphs.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII (OI13) is an autosomal recessive bone fragility disorder caused by deficient BMP1 activity. It is characterized by recurrent fractures, which may be present at birth or begin with weight bearing and mainly affect the lower limbs. Some patients also have bone deformities, severe short stature, joint hyperextensibility, and umbilical hernia. Bone mineral density has been increased in some patients and normal or decreased in others.

paragraphs.text: Munns et al. (2004) described 3 unrelated children with an apparently new bone fragility disorder associated with an idiopathic mineralization defect. Recurrent lower limb fractures began with weight bearing. Radiographs showed increased metaphyseal trabeculation, normal to increased cortical thickness, and no evidence of rickets or osteomalacia. Peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) showed elevated radial cortical thickness and volumetric bone mineral density (BMD). Iliac bone biopsy showed a paucity of the birefringent lamellar bone pattern. On quantitative histomorphometry, there was osteomalacia with a prolonged mineralization lag time and a decreased mineral apposition rate. There was no biochemical evidence of abnormal calcium or phosphate metabolism. Munns et al. (2004) concluded that this was a bone fragility disorder of moderate severity that tends to cause lower extremity fractures and is associated with osteoid accumulation due to an intrinsic mineralization defect. The patients lacked the phenotypic, radiologic, and histomorphometric features of osteogenesis imperfecta, idiopathic juvenile osteoporosis, and mild autosomal dominant osteopetrosis.

paragraphs.text: Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) reported 2 affected sibs born to Egyptian parents who were first cousins and unaffected. The proband (II-3) was a 15-year-old girl referred with a history of recurrent fractures and bone deformities; she had had a tibial fracture at birth. On examination she had a triangular face, broad forehead, wide palpebral fissures, long eyelashes, faint blue sclerae, long philtrum, thin lips, and prominent ears. She had delayed gross motor development but normal mental development, and no dentinogenesis imperfecta. Other findings included a large umbilical hernia, generalized hypotonia, muscle wasting, nocturnal enuresis, and generalized hirsutism, without skin hyperextensibility or bruising. Skeletal findings included bowing of the humerus, radius, and ulna, arachnodactyly, hyperextensibility of the elbow, wrist, and interphalangeal joints, limited knee movement, kyphoscoliosis, and pectus carinatum. Radiographs showed platyspondyly, generalized decreased bone density, and wormian bones. She had short stature (-11.5 SD), low weight, and microcephaly (-3.0 SD). Alkaline phosphatase was slightly elevated, and hearing was normal.

paragraphs.text: In a Korean patient with OI, Cho et al. (2015) identified compound heterozygous variants in the BMP1 gene by whole-exome sequencing. One was a c.808A-G transition resulting in a met270-to-val (M270V) substitution. The other was a c.1297G-T transversion that caused skipping of exon 10. The patient had umbilical hernia, frequent fractures, markedly short stature, delayed motor development, scoliosis, and radial head dislocation. Both variants were hypofunctional in a zebrafish assay.
